eesel AI, Decagon, Teammates.ai

### Cons
**My take:** the best-value published pricing in the category and the smartest autonomy model, but check the per-response meter against your average handle time before you commit. If most of your tickets take one reply, it is very cheap. If they take six, do the math first.

**Whose queue does it own, what does it do when it is not sure, and can you compute the bill** tells you everything, and it takes about ten minutes to answer for any vendor here.

For a customer support queue, [eesel AI](https://www.eesel.ai/ai-helpdesk-agent), Decagon and Teammates.ai. For day-to-day operations across tools, Vellum. For your own team's admin, Lindy or Asana. For building it yourself, Relevance AI. For internal request handling, Ema or Cassidy. And if you are one person doing everything, Sintra at $15.60 a month is a genuinely good place to find out whether any of this helps you.

And if your problem is specifically support, the practical next read is [AI helpdesk software](https://www.eesel.ai/blog/best-ai-helpdesk-software-2026), followed by the roundup of [AI agent examples](https://www.eesel.ai/blog/ai-agent-examples) running in production today.

If routing is the bottleneck rather than answering, [support ticket triage](https://www.eesel.ai/blog/best-ai-for-support-ticket-triage) is the better starting point.

For a live customer support inbox, [eesel AI](https://www.eesel.ai/ai-helpdesk-agent), Decagon and Teammates.ai are the support-focused picks. For day-to-day operations across tools, Vellum. For a solo founder, Sintra.

The difference matters commercially, because only the first one reduces the amount of work a human has to start. See also the split between an agent and a scripted bot in my [rule-based chatbot comparison](https://www.eesel.ai/blog/ai-agent-vs-rule-based-chatbot).

Anywhere from $15.60 a month for Sintra's yearly bundle to a quote-gated enterprise contract at Decagon. The trap is that the meters are incompatible: per task, per outcome, per conversation, per credit, per seat. [eesel AI](https://www.eesel.ai/pricing) uses one credit per ticket or chat session on a fixed monthly plan from $299 for 500 credits, with no seat fee, which is the easiest one to forecast.

Teammates.ai gives 10 credits a month free, Cassidy's free tier includes 10,000 credits and five agents, and Relevance AI keeps agents unlimited even on Free. eesel gives 100 free credits with no card, which covers 100 tickets or chats.

What makes the difference is confidence routing and a clean escalation path, which is why I would read up on [tier-1 deflection](https://www.eesel.ai/blog/ai-for-tier-1-support-deflection) and [ticket triage](https://www.eesel.ai/blog/ticket-triage) before you set an autonomy target.

Its current pricing page says anything with outside impact waits for approval. **Workforce AI view:** Lindy is a strong shortlist choice when Slack is the team's delegation surface. Workforce AI begins with the owner's meeting, inbox, text, and WhatsApp work. Current costPlus lists $29.99 per user monthly; official documentation still shows an older $49.99 figure Watch forThe live pricing page and documentation disagree on entry price and inbox allowances. Confirm checkout terms. Credits are pooled by seat and work can pause when the pool runs out.
3. 03 Sintra AI [Official source](https://sintra.ai/ai-team) Best for: solo owners and small teams that want a ready-made roster of role helpers Sintra X includes twelve helpers for business functions, shared Brain AI context, scheduled tasks, custom helpers, and connected apps. It is approachable when the work is easy to divide into recognizable marketing, content, sales, support, and admin roles. **Workforce AI view:** Sintra is attractive when a bundle of specialist helpers matches the work. Workforce AI is shaped around one continuous owner-side role across client operations. Current costSintra X lists $97 monthly or $468 yearly in the official help center; live promotions vary Watch forCredits vary by action and the helpers stop when credits run out. Approval language is broad rather than one universal technical boundary, so inspect every automation that can send, publish, or change a connected system.
4. 04 Teammates.ai [Official source](https://teammates.ai/help/getting-started/platform-overview) Best for: businesses with a defined customer service, top-of-funnel sales, or first-round recruiting workload Teammates.ai offers Raya for customer service, Adam for sales, and Sara for recruiting. Published channels span phone, email, live chat, WhatsApp, social messaging, LinkedIn, and live video interviews. The three roles share context and a credit pool. **Workforce AI view:** Teammates.ai covers specialized front-line roles. Workforce AI keeps the owner between the AI employee and the owner's clients. Current costFree tier; paid plans begin at $25 monthly, but official pages disagree on included credits Watch forThe product is designed for autonomous customer-facing work within configured policies, with escalation to people. Test knowledge quality, refund or account-change permissions, outreach consent, hiring review, escalation recall, and channel failure before live volume.
5. 05 Asana AI Teammates [Official source](https://asana.com/product/ai/ai-teammates) Best for: teams whose projects, decisions, permissions, and daily collaboration already live in Asana Asana AI Teammates are prebuilt or custom agents that can be assigned work inside Asana projects. They use Work Graph context, project permissions, memories, approved document integrations, and checkpoints while creating, reviewing, researching, or analyzing team work. **Workforce AI view:** Asana is the natural choice when the project board is the company's operating center. Workforce AI follows owner work through meetings, inbox, private messaging, and connected context. Current costAvailable as an add-on to Starter, Advanced, Enterprise, and Enterprise+; contact sales Watch forThe value depends on clean Asana projects and permission discipline. Teams must coach the role, maintain examples and access, review checkpoints, and monitor the pooled AI Request allowance.
6. 06 Relevance AI [Official source](https://relevanceai.com/workforce) Best for: teams that want to design custom agents and multi-agent systems on a visual canvas Relevance AI lets a builder create agents, equip them with tools, connect them into workforces, and monitor their tasks. The self-serve plans support experimentation and scheduled work, while Team adds calling and meeting agents, analytics, and higher concurrency. **Workforce AI view:** Relevance AI rewards a capable builder with broad flexibility. Workforce AI reduces that design job for a narrower small-business operating pattern. Current costFree; Pro is $29 monthly; Team is $349 monthly, with action and model usage Watch forThe builder owns instructions, tools, handoffs, tests, limits, and ongoing debugging. Each connection can auto-run, require approval, or let the agent decide, so review safety is only as strong as the workforce design.
7. 07 Artisan [Official source](https://www.artisan.co/) Best for: sales teams that want a specialized AI BDR for outbound research, campaigns, replies, and booking Artisan's Ava is an outbound sales teammate that finds and enriches leads, runs personalized campaigns, works with CRM and calendar systems, handles replies, and books meetings. The platform is a focused revenue product rather than a general business coworker. **Workforce AI view:** Artisan is the sharper choice for outbound pipeline. Workforce AI covers broader owner-side client operations and does not replace a dedicated sales campaign platform. Current costPublic pricing is not listed; request a scoped quote Watch forCampaign strategy, exclusions, consent, domain reputation, account ownership, claims, and handoff rules need human ownership. Approval mode can hold replies for a click or allow sending, so set that choice per campaign before launch.
9. 09 CrewAI [Official source](https://crewai.com/pricing) Best for: engineering teams that want to build, deploy, observe, and govern their own multi-agent workflows CrewAI combines an open agent framework with a visual editor and managed platform. Teams can build crews and structured flows, connect custom tools and triggers, expose workflows through APIs or Slack and Teams chat, and add tracing, tests, and guardrails. **Workforce AI view:** CrewAI is the right kind of power for a team that wants to engineer its own system. Workforce AI is intended to be hired and managed as a finished owner-side product. Current costBasic is free for 50 workflow executions monthly; Enterprise pricing is custom Watch forThis is infrastructure for creating teammates, not a finished small-business role. The team owns code or visual design, model choice, data access, deployment, monitoring, costs, and human review behavior.
10. 10 Sembly AI [Official source](https://www.sembly.ai/pricing/) Best for: individuals and teams that need meeting capture, searchable history, structured notes, tasks, and meeting-derived documents Sembly attends Zoom, Google Meet, Microsoft Teams, and Webex to produce transcripts, summaries, detected tasks, risks, insights, and documents. Pro adds multi-meeting chat, shared workspaces, consent tracking, automations, and longer history. **Workforce AI view:** Sembly is a focused choice when the meeting record is the job. Workforce AI adds a live Zoom avatar and carries supported context into owner-approved inbox and follow-up work. Current costBasic is $17 monthly; Pro is $29 per user monthly, with lower annual rates Watch forSembly is centered on meeting intelligence. Review detected tasks, owners, dates, consent settings, retention, and any workspace automation that exports notes or tasks into another system.
